Our serviceable obtainable market for enterprise AI will grow from $50B to $150B in the next 5 years.

variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time (future projection)

A metric showing adoption of a new, strategic feature or product line

Justifying a premium valuation by showing a strong core and high growth potential.

variable_elements.secondary_metric: A collection of logos or icons representing the fragmented alternatives (competitors, point solutions, legacy systems).

Your company's logo

records.core_message: Our platform is superior to the competition, offering more critical capabilities at a significantly lower total cost of ownership (TCO).

shows.specific_content: A comparison table showing Snowflake versus a competitor, 'Managed Spark'. It compares them on three qualitative features ('Self-Optimizing', 'Fully Managed Service', 'One Platform Across Stack') where Snowflake has all three (indicated by checkmarks) and the competitor has none (indicated by X's). records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this 'Us vs. Them' pattern to prove superiority over a direct competitor or alternative. The slide establishes a clear narrative by first comparing a checklist of qualitative features, showing where 'we' have capabilities that 'they' lack. This builds a foundation of functional advantage. It then culminates in a single, powerful quantitative metric (like cost, performance, or ROI) that summarizes the overall benefit, making the choice obvious. This combination of qualitative 'what' and quantitative 'how much better' is a highly effective way to create a strong competitive moat.
works_for: Our CRM is easier to use and 20% cheaper than Salesforce for SMBs.
Our security software detects threats 5x faster than the legacy solution.
Compared to building in-house, our platform reduces development time by 60%.
We offer end-to-end encryption and compliance features that our main competitor lacks.
Our electric vehicle has a 25% longer range and charges faster than the leading competitor.
Our marketing automation tool has native integrations that competitors require expensive add-ons for.
Why choose us over AWS Lambda? We offer better performance with no cold starts and lower overall cost.
Our solution provides a unified dashboard, unlike the fragmented tools of our competitors, saving 10 hours per week.

variable_elements.comparison_basis: Direct comparison against a named competitor or alternative solution

records.abstract_pattern: This pattern visualizes a company's commitment to continuous, accelerating improvement in a core value metric over time. It uses a timeline anchored by key product or technology generations to show past progress as a foundation for future, even greater gains. Any company can use this to build confidence in its long-term vision and technology roadmap, framing its product not as a static solution but as an evolving platform that delivers compounding value. It transforms a history of innovation into a promise for the future.
works_for: Our AI models get exponentially more accurate with each new version.
The energy efficiency of our hardware doubles with every product generation.
Our platform's processing speed has consistently increased, and our next release will be the biggest leap yet.
We are driving down the cost per transaction for our customers through continuous software optimization.
Our commitment to R&D means our drug discovery platform identifies candidates faster with each update.
The time-to-value for our customers is decreasing at an accelerating rate.
Our security platform detects more threats with higher accuracy with every engine update.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A key performance or efficiency ratio (e.g., Price/Performance, Speed, Accuracy, Efficiency).
variable_elements.time_dimension: A timeline marked by key product generations, technology milestones, or years.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison of the company's own performance against itself over time.

must_have: A key performance metric that can be shown to improve over time.
A defined set of historical and future product/technology milestones that can be tied to performance gains.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a clear, positive, and ideally accelerating trend. The milestones should logically connect to the improvements.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: At least one past and one future milestone (3+ total points are better to show a curve).

ideal_for: When you need to demonstrate a long-term competitive advantage rooted in technology.
To justify a premium price by showing superior value and future improvements.
When introducing a new product generation and putting it in a historical context of innovation.
To build investor confidence in the company's R&D strategy and future growth potential.
To reassure customers that they are investing in a platform that won't become obsolete.
When you want to frame your company as an innovation leader in your category.
avoid_when: If your product's value proposition is static and not based on performance improvements.
If you don't have a credible story for future innovation or your progress has plateaued.
If your business is services-based rather than technology or product-driven.

records.title: Committed to Leading Price Performance

records.core_message: Our pace of product innovation is not just growing, it's accelerating dramatically, creating a compounding advantage and widening our competitive moat.

shows.specific_content: A bar chart showing a significant increase in 'Product Velocity' over three fiscal years (FY24, FY25, FY26+). The bar for FY25 is labeled with '+2X' and upward arrows, indicating a doubling from FY24. The bar for FY26+ is taller and has a gradient fade, suggesting a future projection of continued acceleration.

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to demonstrate that a key operational capability, such as innovation, sales efficiency, or data processing, is not just improving but accelerating over time. It uses a simple bar chart with a prominent multiplier callout to emphasize a step-change in performance between two periods. It often includes a forward-looking, visually distinct bar (e.g., faded or outlined) to signal that this acceleration is expected to continue, building a narrative of momentum and a widening competitive advantage.
works_for: Our sales team's efficiency has tripled this year, allowing us to scale faster.
We are onboarding new enterprise customers 4x faster than last year.
The number of AI models deployed on our platform is accelerating, proving network effects.
Our rate of shipping new features has doubled, widening our lead over competitors.
The growth in our developer community is compounding year-over-year.
We've doubled our data processing capacity while keeping costs flat.
Our content production has accelerated, making us the dominant voice in the market.
The number of integrations we build per quarter is increasing exponentially.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A key operational or innovation metric (e.g., features shipped, models deployed, integrations built, customers onboarded).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time.

must_have: A quantifiable metric for an operational process (e.g., number of features shipped, number of integrations built, number of patents filed).
Time-series data for this metric over at least two completed periods.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a clear acceleration or step-change between at least two periods. A simple upward trend is not enough; the rate of growth itself must be increasing.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 3+ time periods (e.g., last year, this year, next year's projection).

ideal_for: When you need to prove your R&D or operational engine is a key competitive advantage.
To justify increased investment in product or engineering by showing accelerating returns.
To build a narrative of momentum and market leadership that competitors can't match.
When shifting the story from 'what' you've built to 'how fast' you can innovate.
To counter claims that your innovation has slowed down or that competitors are catching up.
In an investor or board update to showcase operational excellence.
avoid_when: When your growth is linear or slowing down.
When the metric being shown is not clearly linked to business value (i.e., it's a vanity metric).
When you cannot quantify the metric in a believable or defensible way.

records.title: Product Velocity

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to translate technical innovation into clear business value. The structure explicitly identifies a common customer pain point, introduces the company's specific feature or technology as the direct solution, and then proves its effectiveness with a compelling, quantifiable outcome. This 'Problem-Solution-Benefit' framework is highly effective for demonstrating a strong ROI, justifying product superiority, and establishing thought leadership by showing, not just telling, how you solve real-world problems better, faster, or cheaper.
works_for: Our new algorithm reduces cloud storage costs by 50%.
Our automated fraud detection system catches 30% more fraudulent transactions.
Our supply chain optimization software reduces delivery times by 2 days.
Our developer tools increase engineering velocity by 25%.
Our marketing automation platform improves lead conversion by 15%.
Our security platform blocks 99.9% of zero-day threats, a 10% improvement over competitors.
Our CRM's AI assistant cuts down data entry time by 80%.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Customer Problem (Qualitative Pain Point)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Quantified Outcome (e.g., speed, cost, rank)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicit before-and-after comparison (Problem vs. Outcome)

must_have: A list of well-understood customer pain points
Specific company products or features that address each pain point
Quantifiable metrics demonstrating the positive impact of the solution (e.g., percentage improvement, multiplier, cost savings, ranking)
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: Needs a clear one-to-one mapping between a problem, a solution, and a significant, positive outcome. The outcome data must be compelling and easy to grasp.
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 2-3 examples to establish a pattern of innovation and problem-solving.

ideal_for: When proving that R&D investments are creating tangible customer value.
To translate complex technical features into simple business benefits (faster, cheaper, better).
To establish technical superiority and thought leadership in a specific domain.
When justifying a premium price by demonstrating a clear and superior ROI.
To differentiate from competitors by showcasing unique, effective solutions.
In a product-focused section of a pitch to prove product-market fit with hard data.
avoid_when: When your product's benefits are primarily qualitative and lack hard numbers.
If your improvements are only marginal and not compelling enough to highlight.
When you cannot directly link a specific feature to solving a specific, recognized problem.

We are setting the standard for sustainable manufacturing in our sector.

variable_elements.time_dimension: Implicit progression of influence (e.g., from participation to leadership).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly positions the company as a leader relative to others in the industry.

must_have: Evidence of significant contributions to an industry standard, open-source project, or community
Proof of leadership roles (e.g., hosting events, chairing committees, authoring key proposals)
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs a list of 2-4 distinct, escalating examples of influence or contribution

ideal_for: When you need to establish your company as a thought leader, not just a product vendor.
To demonstrate a non-obvious competitive moat built on ecosystem influence.
When justifying your strategic importance to the broader industry.
To build trust with a technical or developer-focused audience by showing commitment to open standards.
When you are trying to create or define a new market category.
To show you are a good citizen in an open-source community.
avoid_when: If your contributions are minor or on par with many competitors.
When your audience is purely focused on financial metrics or product features.
If you are an early-stage company that hasn't yet established a significant industry presence.

It establishes a simple framework for understanding a complex space by breaking it down into its core components. Any company can use this to introduce the key pillars of their strategy, the primary use cases for their product, or the main segments of the market they address. We serve three core customer segments: small businesses, mid-market, and enterprise.
Our marketing automation tool drives acquisition, engagement, and retention.
Our investment strategy is balanced across growth, value, and income assets.

Our AI model handles text, image, and audio inputs.
Our business operates on three principles: speed, quality, and cost-efficiency.

variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly, a unified offering vs. a fragmented market of point solutions.

must_have: A clear, accepted categorization of the market, product capabilities, or customer use cases into (typically three) distinct pillars.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs multiple categories

ideal_for: Introducing the core pillars of your product strategy.
Explaining the breadth of your platform's capabilities in a simple way.
Segmenting a complex market to show how you address each part.
Setting up a narrative about how you unify previously separate functions.
Defining the key use cases your product solves for customers.
Visually representing the core values or principles of your company.

When your product or strategy is focused on a single, narrow function.
When the categories are not well-defined or easily understood by the audience.

It visually communicates breadth, integration, and the idea that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. This framework is used to position a product as a comprehensive, unified solution rather than a collection of point tools, showing how different use cases are all supported by a common, powerful core.
works_for: Our marketing cloud provides a single solution for email, social, advertising, and analytics.
Our operating system powers everything from mobile to desktop to cloud services.
Our financial platform supports consumer banking, investing, lending, and business services.
Our design suite covers vector graphics, photo editing, UI/UX design, and video production.
Our logistics network handles everything from first-mile pickup to last-mile delivery.

Our security platform provides endpoint, network, and cloud protection from a single console.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Product/Capability Pillars
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Foundational Layer/Technology
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Internal components of a single platform

must_have: A defined set of 3-5 major product categories or key use cases
A core technology, brand, or platform concept that unifies them
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: needs multiple categories that can be logically grouped as pillars on a foundation

ideal_for: Explaining your product architecture to strategic or technical audiences.
Pivoting the company narrative from a single product to a multi-product platform.
Showing how different features or business lines are interconnected and synergistic.
Justifying a higher price point by demonstrating comprehensive value.
Arguing against point solutions by showing an integrated alternative.
Introducing a new, unifying layer to your existing product suite.
avoid_when: Your product is a single-feature point solution.
Your different products are not actually integrated and are just a bundle.
You are pitching a very early-stage idea that hasn't been built yet.

records.abstract_pattern: This slide pattern visualizes a company's innovation pipeline or product portfolio maturity. It uses a matrix to track multiple initiatives (products, features, or projects) as they progress through a defined set of lifecycle stages, such as launch, adoption, and monetization. This framework allows a company to demonstrate a healthy and balanced portfolio, showing which initiatives are established, which are gaining traction, and which represent future opportunities. It's a powerful way to prove a systematic approach to growth and de-risk future revenue by showing it's not dependent on a single bet.
works_for: Our platform strategy is working, with new modules being adopted and monetized by our customer base.
We have a clear pipeline of new drugs, with several moving from clinical trials to market launch.
Our investments in R&D are paying off, with a clear path from innovation to commercial success.
Our expansion into new markets is progressing, with early regions already contributing to profit.
We are successfully incubating and scaling new business lines to diversify our revenue streams.
Our new AI features are moving from launch to adoption and will soon be major revenue contributors.
This shows our engine for growth: we consistently launch, validate, and scale new value for customers.

variable_elements.primary_metric: The products, features, or initiatives being tracked.
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The defined stages of maturity or progression (e.g., Launch, Adoption, Monetization).
variable_elements.time_dimension: A point-in-time snapshot showing progress through stages.
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison of multiple internal initiatives against a standardized maturity framework.

must_have: A list of distinct products, features, or strategic initiatives.
A defined set of 3-4 maturity stages.
A quantifiable definition for achieving each stage (e.g., 'Adoption' = >10% of users).
Status data for each initiative against each stage.
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: multiple_categories with a point-in-time snapshot status, showing a distribution of items across different stages to illustrate a healthy pipeline.

ideal_for: When proving that R&D investment is translating into future growth opportunities.
When shifting the narrative from a single-product company to a multi-product platform company.
In an investor day or board meeting to showcase the health of the product pipeline.
To de-risk the company's future by showing multiple 'shots on goal' for growth.
To explain a long-term growth strategy based on continuous innovation and adoption.
When justifying future investment by showing a track record of moving products from launch to impact.
avoid_when: You only have one primary product or feature.
Your new initiatives have failed to gain any meaningful adoption.
You cannot create clear, quantifiable definitions for the maturity stages.

It visually maps each initiative's current stage, from initial launch to adoption and finally to significant business impact (e.g., revenue contribution). This framework effectively communicates a 'pipeline of value,' demonstrating to stakeholders that the company has a systematic process for innovation and that future growth is supported by tangible assets that are already maturing.

We are successfully expanding into new geographic markets, with Europe now showing early traction and Asia targeted for next year's growth.

variable_elements.primary_metric: The initiatives being tracked (e.g., Products, Features, R&D Projects, Market Segments)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: The stages of the maturity lifecycle (e.g., R&D -> GA -> Adoption -> Monetization)
variable_elements.time_dimension: Progression through a series of discrete maturity stages
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Comparison of multiple initiatives against a standardized lifecycle framework

must_have: A list of distinct products, features, or strategic initiatives

Status data for each initiative against each stage of the lifecycle

To justify R&D spending by showing the path from investment to revenue contribution.
To demonstrate a systematic approach to innovation and market expansion.
In an investor day or board meeting to give a high-level status of strategic priorities.

If you lack a clear, repeatable process for product development and rollout.

variable_elements.time_dimension: A future time period (e.g., next fiscal year, next 18 months)
